National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
953 AM EDT Thu Oct 29 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Dense Fog Advisory will expire at 10 AM as fog is quickly
dissipating.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Above normal temperatures through Friday, then seasonable 
  with increasing clouds this weekend. 

- 2) Rain chances remain uncertain for the first half of next 
  week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Above normal temperatures through Friday, then 
seasonable with increasing clouds this weekend. 

The Dense Fog Advisory in effect for parts of the Shenandoah
Valley and Potomac Highlands this morning will be allowed to
expire at 10AM. The increasing daytime heating is causing fog to
dissipate, though some patchy valley fog will linger west of
I-81 as fog lifts to stratus, then burns off by around noon.

After the clouds break, mixing on these light southwest winds
should allow temperatures to reach into the lower to middle 70s
(60s mountains). Low temperatures tonight will be seasonable
in the 40s to lower 50s, but may be rather variable over short 
distances depending on where goes calm and where holds onto a 
light southwest wind. Higher elevations will actually hold on to
more southwest breezes and be poking up into the warming airmass,
and could therefore be some of the warmest spots tonight.

Well above normal temperatures persist Friday, despite a cold
front crossing the region. Cold air advection lags behind this
front, and downsloping flow likely allows for highs to push 
well into the 70s (60s mountains). One caveat is if some 
stratocumulus develops on northwest flow, but the background 
airmass is rather dry so the chance of that happening and it 
having a significant impact on temperatures is limited.

Eventually, some cooler temperatures will filter into the region
Friday night through the weekend. Expect seasonable and dry
conditions as high pressure holds firm, with any precipitation
becoming less likely through at least Sunday evening.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Rain chances remain uncertain for the first 
half of next week. 

Strong high pressure will remain overhead Sunday and only gradually 
drift eastward through the first half of next week. The Mid-Atlantic
will be caught in between more prominent but slow moving troughs
(or closed lows) near Florida/the Bahamas, the Plains, and eastern
Canada. Some models still show potential for a shortwave trough
to ride around the departing ridge, but at this point the chance
for rain has dropped to 30 percent or less between Sunday night
and Tuesday night. Even though conditions may largely remain dry,
expect more cloud cover between onshore surface flow and a warm
advection pattern aloft. Temperatures will likely remain a little
above normal through this period despite the extra clouds. The 
Plains trough may eventually increase rain chances Wednesday or 
Thursday as it moves eastward, but its progression is uncertain 
as well.

&&

.AVIATION /13Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Most of the low clouds and fog have burned off, and should be
completely dissipated by 16Z. Light southwest winds through
tonight with VFR expected. Low cloud/fog potential appears 
lower tonight given a persistent albeit light SW wind.

VFR is likely Friday as winds shift to the northwest. Gusts of
20-25 knots are likely around midday into mid afternoon as a dry
cold front crosses. Winds become lighter Friday night into
Saturday while shifting to the north, with light east to calm
winds Saturday night as high pressure builds.

Significant weather is unlikely Sunday and Monday as high pressure 
moves eastward. However, some low chances of sub-VFR ceilings and a 
few rain showers exist Monday depending on how the weather pattern 
evolves.

&&

.MARINE...
Light south to southwest winds are expected through tonight,
though a few gusts around 15 knots are possible at times. A dry
cold front will shift winds to the northwest Friday, with near
shore and narrower waterways having the potential to see gusts
to near 20 knots at times. Northerly channeling Friday night may
prompt Small Craft Advisories before diminishing Saturday. Winds
then shift to the east Saturday night as high pressure builds.

Light winds will likely continue Sunday and Monday as high pressure 
gradually moves offshore.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal anomalies remain elevated, though have been slowly
decreasing so far tonight. Some fluctuation is possible over the
next 12-24 hours which could send vulnerable shoreline to near
minor flood stage this evening.

Offshore flow decreases tide levels Friday into Saturday. Winds
turn back around out of the south at low speeds which could
cause a modest rebound in tides by Sunday.
